subject: Computer Networking
title: WPA3: Securing Wi-Fi
description: A quick win: understand WPA3: Securing Wi-Fi.

hook.text: Open Wi-Fi networks are dangerous — anyone can sniff your traffic. WPA3 fixes what older standards couldn't.

buildup.text: WPA3 uses Simultaneous Authentication of Equals, making it resistant to offline password-guessing attacks.

discovery.text: Even on public networks, WPA3 encrypts each user's session individually. No more shared-key snooping.

twist.text: WPA2 was considered secure for years until the KRACK attack exposed a critical handshake flaw in 2017.

climax.text: WPA3 adoption is growing but slow. Most devices and routers still default to WPA2 for compatibility.

punchline.text: WPA3 makes Wi-Fi safer, one upgrade at a time.

quiz.question: What attack exposed a critical flaw in WPA2?

details.summary: WPA3 replaces WPA2 with stronger Wi-Fi security, using Simultaneous Authentication of Equals for password-based key exchange that protects against offline dictionary attacks.
details.whyItMatters: WPA2's vulnerabilities like KRACK showed that Wi-Fi security needed a fundamental upgrade. WPA3 protects even weak passwords from offline cracking and secures previously unprotected open networks.
takeaways: SAE key exchange resists offline dictionary attacks on passwords
Open networks get individual encryption via OWE

faq.question: How does WPA3 protect against password cracking?
faq.answer: WPA3 uses SAE, a zero-knowledge proof protocol that verifies the password without transmitting or deriving a crackable hash. Each authentication attempt must happen interactively with the access point, making offline dictionary attacks impossible. Even simple passwords get strong protection.

faq.question: Do I need new hardware for WPA3?
faq.answer: Some older devices received WPA3 through firmware updates, but most require hardware that includes WPA3 support. Wi-Fi 6 devices generally support WPA3 natively. WPA3-transition mode allows WPA2 and WPA3 devices to coexist on the same network during the upgrade period.
